candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is melanoma. The clinical record describes a 27-year-old with a prior 5 mm thick melanoma who develops a lung mass and hyoid bone lesion. The lung mass responded to VCD/IE chemotherapy, but the hyoid lesion grew and new neck adenopathy appeared mid-treatment, suggesting the hyoid/neck disease is a distinct entity—most consistent with metastatic melanoma recurrence. C001 names Ewing sarcoma/PNET, which was the initial molecular interpretation of the lung lesion but is not the final unifying diagnosis requested. Ewing sarcoma/PNET is a related but incompatible final diagnostic entity compared to melanoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Ewing sarcoma/PNET is the initial working diagnosis based on molecular studies, but the clinical course (chemotherapy response of lung mass, progression of hyoid lesion and new neck adenopathy, prior thick melanoma history) points to melanoma as the unifying final diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Complex case with two synchronous lesions; the lung lesion may represent Ewing sarcoma/PNET while the hyoid/neck lesion likely represents metastatic melanoma—the reference diagnosis 'melanoma' likely refers to the overall unifying or dominant final diagnosis given the clinical history
Nondiagnostic hyoid biopsy limits certainty; the final diagnosis of melanoma is inferred from clinical context and treatment response pattern rather than confirmed histology of the hyoid lesion
